subject: gargoyle
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: cathedral gargoyle crouched on a ledge.
Style: gothic stone carving.

spec.name: Cathedral Gargoyle
spec.description: A chunky, chisel-faceted stone gargoyle crouched on a weathered cathedral ledge, wings half-open, grinning with fangs and gripping the stone edge with its claws.
spec.layout: Everything is one gothic stone carving: blocky, faceted primitives in a grey stone palette, with moss, soot and chips as their own small parts. The ledge is a stone cornice slab, 1.7 wide, 0.3 tall and 1.76 deep, at z -0.88..0.88. Its front edge has a stepped moulding and three corbel blocks under it, and its top has a shallow rain-gutter groove. The gargoyle crouches on its centre line, with the pelvis low and back at z -0.2 and the shoulders high and forward at z 0.3. The spine arches up from pelvis to chest, the neck is short and thick, and the head is thrust forward and slightly down at z 0.58..0.95, with its top at about y 1.45. Hands are planted on the ledge at z about 0.7. Hind legs are digitigrade: thigh forward and up, shin back and down, flat clawed feet at z about 0.2. The tail runs back from the rump, curls along the ledge to the model's right (-X) and ends in a diamond spade tip at about [-0.72, 0.45, -0.4]. Bat wings are half-open: each arm bone rises and sweeps out to the side, three finger bones fan back from the wrist, and a thick stone-slab membrane stretches between them and to the flank. The wings peak at y about 1.6 and span x ±1.15. Identity cues are built big: a heavy beetle brow, a wide grinning mouth with a separate upper jaw and lower jaw and 4-6 chunky fangs, two swept-back ridged horns, big pointed ears, a pug nose with flared nostrils, and a stone beard or chin tuft. Eye sockets are deep and carved, with an amber glowing eyeball inside. The body gets stone blocks and chisel ridges: a row of spinal knobs, plated belly bands, ribs, knuckle studs and brow ridges. Colour goes by place: lighter stone on top and front faces, darker stone below and in recesses. Moss sits on upward faces of the ledge, shoulders, back and wing tops. Soot and water-stain streaks run down the ledge front and under the chin. A few dark crack lines and pale chip patches sit as thin parts seated on the surface. Every surface is a flat colour.

parts.builds: The cathedral ledge the gargoyle crouches on. A stone slab, 1.7 wide, 0.3 tall and 1.76 deep (stone, with a darker stoneDark base course), topped by a slightly overhanging cornice slab (stoneLight) with a stepped moulding on the front and side edges. Three or four corbel blocks (stoneDark) under the front edge. A shallow rain-gutter groove across the top (stoneDeep) and a small square plinth block (stone) under the gargoyle's body. Masonry joints are thin mortar-coloured strips on the front and sides, with a few offset block faces. Moss patches (moss, mossDark) as low flat blobs on upward faces and the corners. Soot and waterStain streaks running down the front face under the gargoyle. Two rust-coloured iron cramps on top, chips and cracks (crack) as small thin parts, and a few pale chip patches. Keep it simpler than the gargoyle and well inside its box, and do not build anything above y 0.36 except small moss and the plinth.
parts.attaches: Top face at the ledgeTop mount (y 0.3). The gargoyle's feet, hands and tail rest on it; all geometry is static on the root joint pelvis.

parts.builds: Torso and tail of the gargoyle. A hunched loft or sweep body riding pelvis, spine2 and chest: heavy rounded-box pelvis and haunches mass, a deep barrel chest with high shoulder blocks (shoulder mass at the shoulderL and shoulderR mounts, radius about 0.2), and a tucked belly. Colours: stone body, stoneLight on the top and front, stoneDark on the belly. Carved details: a row of 7-9 spinal knobs and ridge blades (stoneLight) from tail base to neck, 5-6 pairs of rib arcs on the flanks, 4-5 plated belly bands (stoneDark), and chest pectoral plates. Wing root sockets (stoneDark blocks) at wingRootL and wingRootR. The tail runs from tailRoot through tail1..tail5, tapering from radius 0.1 to 0.04, in a curl to the model's right ending at tailTip with a flat diamond spade tip (stoneLight, with a stoneDark midrib), and small ridge spines along its top. Moss on the back top and shoulder tops (moss), a soot patch near the haunch, a crack or two. The tail rests on the ledge, with its underside at y >= 0.32.
parts.attaches: Neck base meets the head part at neckBase. Arm sockets at shoulderL and shoulderR (the limbs part starts there). Hip sockets at hipL and hipR. Wing roots at wingRootL and wingRootR. Skins over pelvis, spine2, chest and tail1..5, and bears no limb or head geometry.

parts.builds: The hero head, the richest part, on neck1, neck2, head and jaw. A thick neck sweep (stone) from neckBase. A broad blocky skull (stone) with a heavy overhanging beetle brow ridge (stoneLight, with chisel notches) and deep eye sockets (stoneDeep). In each socket sits an amber eyeball (eyeGlow, to be glowed) and a dark slit pupil (soot). A wide flat muzzle with a pug nose block, flared nostril holes (stoneDeep), cheek bones and cheek ruffs. An UPPER jaw on head and a separate LOWER jaw on joint jaw (hinge at jawHinge): the upper lip has 4-6 chunky fangs (fang) with two big canines, and the lower jaw has an underbite row of 4 fangs, a protruding chin and a chunky stone beard tuft (stoneLight over stoneDark), a tongue slab (rust) and a dark mouth interior (stoneDeep). Two big swept-back horns (stoneLight at the base, stoneDark ridges, claw-coloured tips), each curving back and up from the brow, tip at y <= 1.55. Two large pointed bat ears (stone with stoneDark inner slabs), a row of small head ridge blocks, moss on the crown, a soot streak under the chin and crack lines. The face is built forward, with nothing in front of it.
parts.attaches: The neck sweep starts at neckBase (y 1.08, z 0.38) overlapping the chest. The skull centres on headBase [0, 1.2, 0.58] and the lower jaw hinges at jawHinge [0, 1.12, 0.72]. The head faces +Z and tilts slightly down.

parts.builds: All four limbs, built mirrored for left (+X) and right (-X). Arms: shoulderL, elbowL, wristL and handL, and likewise on the right. They are thick sweeps (radius 0.11 at the shoulder down to 0.07 at the wrist) with a muscular upper arm, an elbow knob (stoneLight) and a forearm, ending in big chunky hands planted flat on the ledge at the handL and handR mounts (y about 0.34). Each hand has a palm block and three splayed fingers plus a thumb, with a knuckle stud on each finger and a curved claw (claw) on each tip. Finger and toe digit chains are created by this part as `b.chain` with names like fingerLA1, fingerLA2, fingerLB1... (letters and digits only, role digit, parent handL, handR, footL or footR, 2 joints each). Legs: hipL, kneeL, ankleL and footL, digitigrade and crouched, with a bulky thigh haunch, a knee knob, a shin tapering to the hock and a long flat foot with three forward toes and claws (toeLA1 etc., parent footL), planted at y 0.3-0.34 on the ledge. The right side mirrors. Stone colours: limbs stone, with stoneLight top planes, stoneDark undersides, chisel-groove stripes, a moss patch on the thighs, and scuffs of soot near the feet.
parts.attaches: Arm tops start at shoulderL and shoulderR (inside the torso shoulder mass). Hand claws touch the ledge at handL and handR. Hip tops start at hipL and hipR. Feet rest at footL and footR on the ledgeTop height y 0.3. Rides joints shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand, hip, knee, ankle and foot on both sides, plus its own digit joints.

parts.builds: Two bat-style wings, built mirrored for left (+X) and right (-X), half-open and swept up and out in the rest pose. Each wing's arm bone is a chunky sweep (stone, radius 0.07 tapering to 0.05) through wingArmL, wingElbowL and wingWristL, with a shoulder block, an elbow knuckle and a wrist claw hook (claw). Three finger bones (wingRib, radius about 0.03 tapering to 0.012, created as chains named wingFingerL1, wingFingerL2, wingFingerL3 with 2 joints each, parent wingWristL, role wing, and likewise wingFingerR1..3) fan back and out from the wrist, ending in small claw-coloured tips at about [1.1, 1.55, -0.7], [1.05, 1.0, -0.85] and [0.85, 0.65, -0.75], mirrored for the right. The membrane is a thick stone-slab skin between the arm, the fingers and the body flank (wing colour, with a scalloped trailing edge, thickness about 0.03), with raised ribs (wingRib) running along each finger, panel seam lines (stoneDeep), a few carved chips, moss along the upper arm tops (moss), and a soot or waterStain gradient near the lower edge. The overall span is about x ±1.15, with its highest point at y about 1.6 and the lowest edge above y 0.6, and nothing in front of z 0.2.
parts.attaches: Arm bones start at wingRootL and wingRootR on the torso shoulder sockets (chest joint). The wrist is at wingWristL and wingWristR. The inner membrane edge attaches to the flank near the pelvis, behind the arms, without blocking the limbs.

I'm planning the gargoyle's pose and proportions crouched on a stone ledge, roughly 1.2 meters tall with wings half-spread back and upward, working out how wide the overall silhouette should be with limbs and wings extended.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton: pelvis as root, spine chain up through chest to neck and head, shoulders feeding into arms gripping the ledge edge, haunches bent into crouched legs with feet planted on the ledge, wing roots branching out from the upper back, and a tail curling off the pelvis down the side. I'm also planning the part split into five pieces -- ledge with cornice and moss detailing, torso with ribs and tail, and a head section with skull, jaws, fangs and horns -- each with its own budget.

Continuing up the chain: neck segments leading to the head, angled forward and slightly down so it's looking outward, with a hinged jaw joint. Then I'm working out the chest and shoulder placement, hunched forward, and planning the arm joints so the hands land planted on the ledge's front edge.

For fingers, I'll let the limb-building logic generate its own digit chains with a consistent naming prefix rather than hardcoding every joint name upfront, keeping the joint list manageable while still giving the rig separated digits.

Now I'm mapping out the bat-style wing geometry: root, elbow, and wrist joints swept upward with fan-shaped finger tips forming the membrane, keeping overall width around 2.2. I'm also figuring out the tail, having it curl back along the rear ledge edge within the body's length span.

I'll swing the tail to the left side instead, extending the ledge a bit to give room, tracing a curved path from the base down and out to a spade-shaped tip near the edge, checking it clears the haunch.

Now I'm working out leg placement for a crouched digitigrade pose, placing hip, knee, and ankle joints so the thigh angles forward-up, the shin folds back-down, and the foot plants flat with toes pointing forward.

Then I'm roughing out the arm joints — shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand — with the elbow bent back, checking that segment lengths stay proportional before mirroring everything to the right side.

Mirroring the right limbs by negating x, I'm placing the head chain next with neck, head, and jaw joints positioned along the vertical axis, skipping separate ear or tongue joints since the horns can stay rigid on the head bone. Then I'm working out the wing skeleton, setting the root at the chest and the elbow and wrist joints rising toward a peak height consistent with the figure's overall 1.7 unit height, and starting to define the wing finger joints.

Now I'm finalizing the overall size bounds, factoring the horns and wing peak into the height, and settling on the depth and width proportions. I'm also drafting the color palette with base stone tones, moss greens, soot, and a glowing eye accent for the gothic stone aesthetic.

Next I'm assigning mount points for the body parts -- pelvis, chest, head, jaw hinge, shoulders -- to position the gargoyle anatomy on the ledge.

Now I'm building the ledge geometry with corbels, plinth, rain-gutter groove, moss and chips, then defining the torso box covering pelvis, spine, chest, ribs, and tail.

I'm setting head box dimensions checking for overhang beyond the ledge front, then sizing the limbs and wings boxes, noting that the wings will overlap the torso at the back, and starting to tally the part budgets.

Now I'm defining the full joint chain and roles—pelvis as spine root, through spine, neck, head, jaw, and tail segments—placing tail joint positions and beginning to compute the bone direction vectors between them.

I'm now thinking through the final layout and visual style notes: a hunched gargoyle with shoulders high, head thrust forward, heavy brow, swept-back horns, pointed ears, fanged grin, and big hands gripping a ledge. I'm noting color placement—moss on upward-facing stone surfaces and shoulders, soot streaks beneath, hollow eyes with amber glow—plus the chunky faceted stone-carving style with chisel marks and masonry lines before writing the final output.

I'm writing the buildLedge function using the Ctx structure, attaching parts to the pelvis bone with flat palette colors, keeping everything within the defined box bounds and adding a slight overhanging cornice detail.

Adding more geometry layers...

I need to check the plinth doesn't clash with the tail, which rests on the ledge underside around y>=0.32. Adjusting the plinth footprint so its edge pulls back to z -0.25 keeps it clear of where the tail extends down toward z -0.45..-0.75, while still supporting the feet and hands at y 0.34.

For the chamfer, I'll add a thin bevel slab below the plinth (y 0.30..0.32, slightly wider, x ±0.48) topped by the plinth itself (y 0.32..0.34, x ±0.44), giving a stepped cornice look.

For moss, I'm using flattened spheres or low-sided cylinders as small patches scattered near the corners and top edges, keeping them above y 0.36 so they don't interfere with the feet placement.

Now I'm adding moss clinging to cornice ledges and small dark drips hanging below the cornice on the front face, plus vertical soot streaks—thin tapering boxes placed on the front face around x -0.1 to 0.2, running down from y 0.22, kept on the body rather than crossing onto the moulding.

Mapping out masonry joints next: horizontal lines across the front at y=0.14, with vertical joints staggered between courses at specific x offsets, repeating the pattern on the side faces and lightly on the back, plus a few slightly protruding stone blocks for texture variation.

Adding a rain-gutter groove and spout notch near the cornice front, plus considering small dentil blocks beneath the moulding to break up the front face detail.

I'm tallying the part budget across base, moulding, corbels, mortar joints, dentils, gutter, plinth, moss, soot, cramps, cracks, and chips to stay near the 120-element limit, trimming dentils down to keep things tight before writing the box helper function.

I also think I'll skip extra toes but add a small rear spur spike on the ankle bone, plus knuckle studs on top of each toe. Then I'm scattering moss patches as flattened blobs along the thigh and shoulder surfaces using the sweep positioning function, and planning thin dark soot scuff disks near the feet on the ledge surface.

Placing soot scuff cylinders near the feet...

Computing arm segment lengths...

For the claw I'll sweep a bezier curve along the chain with radius tapering to a point tip, using flat start and pointed end caps.

Writing groove helper code...

Then I'm adding a moss helper using flattened icosahedron geometry with a scale option for stick elements, plus pale stone-light patches for chip details.

Computing the orientation vectors for the spade extrusion...

Adding a small midrib rod along the spade blade, then working out the body sweep path with pelvis, spine, and chest control points along a catmull curve to shape the tucked belly form.

Still refining rib spacing and taper...

Setting finger tip positions for the left wing and sketching mid-point curves with a slight bow for each sweep before building the actual joint paths.

I'm measuring the arm's leading edge length versus the first finger's length to figure out how to pair them up for the first panel.

Okay, simpler plan: three membrane panels, each defined by two root-to-tip edges — finger1 to finger2, finger2 to finger3, and finger3 to a flank point near the body/tail — forming the wing surface between the digits and down to the body.

Now for panel M0, I'm working out the leading edge between the arm path (root→elbow→wrist) and a second edge connecting root→flank→wrist, forming a kite-like quadrilateral region rather than a simple triangle.

Checking the flank point sits inside the body radius and that no edges dip below the y=0.6 floor — tip claws need to stay small and short so they don't violate that boundary. Now I'm thinking through how the membrane edges should follow the bone/finger chain paths for proper skinning.
